questions.q: What does ALTER TABLE ... ADD do?
options: Adds a new column to an existing table, NULL on every existing row by default
Creates a brand-new table
Adds a new row of data
Adds a new database
questions.explain: A new nullable column simply appears with NULL on every row that already exists, unless given a DEFAULT.

questions.q: Why can ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN fail on a table that already has data?
options: SQL Server checks the existing data, and rejects the change if any row can't fit the new type or constraint
ALTER COLUMN always fails on tables with more than one row
It can only widen columns, never narrow them, by rule
It silently truncates any data that doesn't fit
questions.explain: SQL Server won't silently truncate or corrupt existing data — if even one row doesn't fit the new definition, the whole ALTER is rejected.

questions.q: What happens to a column's data when you run ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN?
options: The column and every value stored in it are permanently removed, for every row
The data is archived automatically to a backup table
Only NULL values are removed; other values are kept in a hidden column
Nothing — DROP COLUMN only removes the column's display name
questions.explain: DROP COLUMN is permanent — there's no undo short of restoring a backup.

questions.q: Which kind of ALTER COLUMN change is usually safest on a table with existing data?
options: Widening a column, such as NVARCHAR(50) to NVARCHAR(100)
Narrowing a column to a smaller size
Changing a text column to an incompatible numeric type
There is no safe ALTER COLUMN change
questions.explain: Growing a column rarely conflicts with existing data, while shrinking or changing type can fail if existing values no longer fit.

questions.q: What might block a DROP COLUMN from succeeding?
options: A default constraint, check constraint, or index still referencing that column
The table having zero rows
The column being nullable
The database being named with a schema prefix
questions.explain: Dependent objects like constraints or indexes on that column must be dropped first before the column itself can be dropped.
